prompt: SCENE: A dark, quiet devotional still life in an unlit room in the evening, with nobody present. One old vinyl record lies flat on a slab of warm honey beige stone, and one short beeswax candle burns just behind it. These two things sit together at the right hand end of a very wide picture, and the rest of the picture is plain warm darkness. The record is shown as a simple emblem of a song, the way a single leaf might stand for a tree: it is not displayed as merchandise, and nothing around it suggests a shop, a delivery or a gift. The camera is low and close to the stone and looks slightly down at the record from about 30 degrees above the surface, level and with no tilt, so the round record appears as a wide, flat, even oval. Behind the stone there is no wall, no window, no back edge of a table and no horizon line: the stone simply falls away into the same darkness. LAYOUT BY PROPORTION: This is a very wide picture that will later be trimmed to an even wider and shorter strip, and gold and cream lettering will be laid over its left side afterwards. The LEFT 60 percent of the frame, from the left edge to 60 percent of the width and from the very top to the very bottom, is an empty, even, near black ground and nothing else. It is a very dark warm brown black, like the darkest roasted coffee seen in shadow, the same from top to bottom and from side to side, with only the faintest fine matte texture, like dark plaster in a dim room. In that left part there is no object, no surface edge, no line, no reflection, no gradient band, no lighter patch, no glow and no visible detail of any kind. It is the calmest and most uniform part of the whole picture. The picture itself lives only in the RIGHT 40 percent of the frame. The lit scene does not have an edge. Moving from right to left, the candlelight on the stone and on the record fades slowly and smoothly, and between 68 percent and 55 percent of the width it dissolves completely into the dark ground, like light running out in a dark room. There is no straight boundary, no panel, no border, no frame, no vignette ring and no oval of light: only a long, soft, natural falloff into darkness. The record is the largest thing in the picture. Its centre is 82 percent of the way across the frame and 62 percent of the way down. Seen at this low angle it is an oval about one third of the frame width wide, reaching from about 66 percent to about 98 percent of the way across, and a little more than one third of the frame height tall, reaching from about 43 percent to about 81 percent of the way down. A thin margin of lit stone shows between the record and the right edge of the frame, and a band of stone shows in front of it along the bottom. The left rim of the record, near 66 percent of the width, is already deep in shadow and shows only as one thin, dim bronze line sinking into the dark. The round label in the middle of the record is about one third of the width of the record, a small flat oval sitting at 82 percent of the way across and 62 percent of the way down. The label is plain matte paper in soft terracotta, the colour of a sun faded clay flower pot, completely blank, with nothing printed, written, drawn or embossed on it, and one small spindle hole at its centre. The single beeswax candle stands on the stone just behind the far right side of the record, centred about 91 percent of the way across. It is a short, stout, honey coloured pillar in a low, plain, unpolished brass holder. Its base is about 42 percent of the way down and the tip of its small steady flame is about 21 percent of the way down. Nothing else is on the stone. LIGHT AND TONE: This picture is a rich, dark background in near black, warm stone and old gold. All the light comes from the upper right: from the candle, helped by a low, soft, warm glow from a small window that is out of the picture above and to the right. The brightest part of the whole frame lies between 80 percent and 90 percent of the width: the honey stone beside the candle, the terracotta label and the nearest grooves of the record. Even there the light is gentle and golden, and nothing is pure white. The stone is warm honey beige, like smooth matte travertine or old limestone, with a fine natural grain and no polish. It is warmly lit near the candle and grows steadily darker toward the left and toward the far distance until it can no longer be told apart from the dark ground. The vinyl is a deep warm brown black with fine concentric grooves, and on the side facing the candle the grooves carry a soft satin sheen as long, calm, curved streaks of bronze and old gold. There is no hard white reflection, no bright wedge of glare and no rainbow sheen on the record. The candle flame is small and calm, a simple teardrop of warm light with no ring, disc or haze around it. Shadows fall to the left and toward the camera, soft and warm, and they merge into the darkness. The colours are near black warm brown, honey stone, beeswax, old gold, dull bronze in the brass and one note of soft terracotta on the label. Nothing is cold, blue, grey or green. The darkness in the left part is flat and even all the way to the top left and bottom left corners, with no extra darkening at the corners and no lighter centre. The mood is warm, reverent, peaceful and precious, like a quiet chapel shelf after evening prayer, never gloomy or frightening. CROPPING: Only the middle band of this picture will be used. A strip of about one ninth of the height is trimmed from the top and the same from the bottom, and the full width is kept. Nothing essential is in the top 15 percent or the bottom 15 percent of the height: above the flame there is only darkness, and below the record there is only stone falling into shadow. The whole record, its whole label, the whole candle and the tip of the flame all sit between 20 percent and 82 percent of the frame height. STYLE: Realistic editorial still life photograph taken on a full frame camera with an 85mm lens from a tripod, by available light only, with no flash and no added studio lighting. The focus is on the label and the near grooves of the record, and the candle just behind is very slightly soft. True photographic detail in the grooves, the stone grain, the wax and the dull brass, with fine natural grain, deep clean shadows and natural colour. The record looks old, played and cared for, not new and not shrink wrapped, and it is a true, smooth, even oval with no warping. Landscape orientation, aspect ratio 21:9. STRICT EXCLUSIONS: There are no people anywhere in the image: no singer, no choir, no musician, no priest, no congregation, no hands, no fingers, no arms, no silhouettes, no shadows of people and no reflections of people. There is no text anywhere in the image: no letters, no numbers, no words, no music notation, no title, no track list, no catalogue number, no ring of small print around the label, no monogram, no logo, no icon, no symbol, no watermark, no caption, no button, no interface element, no border and no frame around the picture. The label on the record is blank. No record sleeve, no album cover, no inner sleeve, no turntable, no tonearm, no stylus, no record player, no speaker, no headphones, no compact disc, no cassette, no telephone, no screen, no musical instrument. No box, no parcel, no envelope, no packaging, no gift wrap, no ribbon, no printed booklet, no book, no card, no price tag. No cross, no crucifix, no rosary, no beads, no bracelet, no necklace, no medal, no jewellery, no statue, no holy picture. No second candle, no cloth, no flowers, no leaves, no cup and no other object of any kind. No halo, no rays or beams of light, no light shafts, no haze, no smoke, no fog, no glowing or ghostly shapes, no lens flare, no sparkles, no floating dust. No split screen, no hard vertical edge and no visible join between the dark ground and the picture. Not bright, not pale, not cream, not cold. Not an illustration, not a painting, not a 3D render, not glossy advertising, not oversaturated, not HDR.
crop: Keep the full width. Keep the central horizontal band whose height is the image width divided by 3: trim 11.1 percent of the height off the top and 11.1 percent off the bottom (keep rows from 11.1 to 88.9 percent).
